\begin{bankpassage}[id=SI12-P2-PHY-S1-G3-4, source={Score-I - Test 12 (09 Mar 2022)}, questions={3-4}]
A person stands on a platform-and-pulley system, as shown in Column-I. The masses of the platform and person are $M$ and $m$ respectively. The rope and pulley is massless. The man can pull on the rope so as to produce one of the situations given in following question. In column-I $W_1$ is tension \& $W_2$ is normal reaction between the man and the platform. Match the possible situations.
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{|p{0.8cm}|p{3.6cm}|p{0.8cm}|p{3.8cm}|p{0.8cm}|p{3.8cm}|}
\hline
 & \centering Column-I & \multicolumn{2}{c|}{Column-II} & \multicolumn{2}{c|}{Column-III}\\
\hline
(I) & \bfigi{66.1}{SI12_p2_phy_s1_para3_4_1.png}\rule{0pt}{35pt} & (i) & $W_2=(2m-M)\dfrac g3$ & (P) & $W_1=(m+M)\dfrac g3$\\
\hline
(II) & \bfigi{77.0}{SI12_p2_phy_s1_para3_4_2.png}\rule{0pt}{45pt} & (ii) & $W_2=(2m-M)\dfrac g2$ & (Q) & $W_1=(m+M)\dfrac g2$\\
\hline
(III) & \bfigi{67.5}{SI12_p2_phy_s1_para3_4_3.png}\rule{0pt}{42pt} & (iii) & $W_2=(m-M)\dfrac g4$ & (R) & $W_1=(m+M)g$\\
\hline
(IV) & \bfigi{52.9}{SI12_p2_phy_s1_para3_4_4.png}\rule{0pt}{33pt} & (iv) & $W_2=(3m-M)\dfrac g4$ & (S) & $W_1=(m+M)\dfrac g4$\\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\end{bankpassage}

The ring is attached to a block B of mass 0.5 kg by means of a light string which passes over a smooth pulley P. Assuming the equilibrium is limiting, if the coefficient of friction ($\mu$) between R and the rod is $\mu = \dfrac{1}{\alpha - \sqrt{\beta}}$ where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the smallest possible integer. Fill the value of ($\alpha$ + $\beta$).\par
\bfig{95.1}{SA02_p2_phy_s3_q07_1.png}
\end{bankq}

A piece of light inextensible thread covers the pulleys, to the ends of the thread we attach identical loads of mass M each. The threads are always taut. A constant force F is exerted on the movable disc as shown in the figure (top view). The thread does not slip relative to the discs.\par
\bfig{63.5}{SA07_p2_phy_s1_q05_1.png}

\opt{D}{The net torque on the fixed disc is zero (or negligibly small).}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=STAR02-P2-PHY-S2-Q06, source={Star Review (Other) - Test 02 (10 Oct 2022)}, paper=2, qno=6, type=multi, subtopic={Circular dynamics}, answer={A,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K1 S3 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: bead on a cord wound around a cylinder with drag | steps: components of velocity; steady motion condition; tangential force balance; speed; radius; check}]
A light inextensible cord is wrapped around a frictionless cylinder of radius $R$ fixed vertically on a floor that is lubricated with oil. A bead of mass $m$ is tied at one end of the cord and the other end $P$ is free as shown by the top view of the situation. Force of viscous drag on the bead due to layer of the lubricating oil is proportional to the speed of the bead and the proportionality constant is $k$. If the free end of the cord is pulled with a constant speed $u$ along the cylinder, the bead eventually acquires a steady motion on a circular path for speed of the bead ($v$) and radius of its circular path $r$ in its steady motion are :\par
\bfig{62.9}{STAR02_p2_phy_s2_q06_1.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$v=u\sqrt{1+\left(\dfrac{mu}{kR}\right)^2}$}
\opt{B}{$v=\dfrac{mu^2}{kR}$}
\opt{C}{$r=\dfrac{mu}{k}$}
\opt{D}{$r=R\sqrt{1+\left(\dfrac{mu}{kR}\right)^2}$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
